title: Minimum Rectangles to Cover Points
statement:
You are given an array `points` of distinct points, where `points[i] = [xi, yi]`, and an integer `w`. You may place any number of rectangles that stand on the x-axis: each one spans horizontally from some `x1` to some `x2` with `x1 <= x2` and `x2 - x1 <= w`, and vertically from `0` up to some height `y2 >= 0`.

A point is covered when it lies inside a rectangle or on its border, and rectangles may overlap. Return the smallest number of rectangles needed so that every point is covered.
notes:
## Intuition

A rectangle can be as tall as we like and its bottom sits on `y = 0`, while every `y` is at least `0`, so heights never matter: a point is covered exactly when its `x` lies in the rectangle's range `[x1, x2]`. The task becomes covering numbers on a line with segments of length `w`. The leftmost uncovered point must be covered by some segment, and the best such segment starts exactly at that point: it covers it and reaches as far right as possible. Repeating that choice is optimal.

## Approach

1. Take the `x` of every point into `xs` and sort it.
2. Start with `rectangles = 0` and `coveredUntil = -1`, since nothing is covered yet.
3. Scan `xs` from left to right. If `x` is beyond `coveredUntil`, open a new rectangle starting at `x`: count it and set `coveredUntil = x + w`.
4. Points with `x <= coveredUntil` are already inside the last rectangle; skip them.
5. Return `rectangles`.

## Example 1, step by step

`points = [[2,1],[1,0],[1,4],[1,8],[3,5],[4,6]]`, `w = 1`, so the sorted `xs` are `[1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4]`.

- `x = 1`: `1 > -1`, open rectangle 1 covering `[1, 2]`.
- `x = 1, 1, 2`: all at most `2`, already covered.
- `x = 3`: `3 > 2`, open rectangle 2 covering `[3, 4]`.
- `x = 4`: covered.

The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for sorting; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(n) for `xs`.

## Pitfalls

- Borders count: a point at exactly `x + w` is covered, so open a rectangle only when `x > coveredUntil`, not `>=`.
- Start `coveredUntil` below every coordinate (`-1`); starting at `0` would treat a point at `x = 0` as covered.
- Several points can share an `x`; they cost nothing extra, and the `y` values are never needed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `xs` | x-coordinates of all points, sorted |
| `rectangles` | rectangles placed so far |
| `coveredUntil` | right edge of the last rectangle placed |
| `x` | the current x-coordinate in the scan |

narration.2: Heights never matter, so keep only each point's x-coordinate.
narration.3: Sort the x-coordinates so the leftmost uncovered point is always the next one seen.
narration.5: Nothing is covered yet; every x is at least 0, so -1 is below all of them.
narration.7: Visit the x-coordinates from left to right.
narration.8: Is this point to the right of the last rectangle?
narration.9: Yes: it needs a new rectangle.
narration.10: Start the rectangle at x so it reaches as far right as allowed, up to x + w.
narration.13: Every point is covered; return how many rectangles were used.
